authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6152 danta explicitly gives Maiya/Palula dān, Gawri dant and northwestern dand “tooth”; its addendum includes aspirated Sindhi dandh. The simple dān/dant/dandh survey forms therefore fit this family. Reviewed comparison: Buksa dand “teeth” (f_jxv5klhb2nns6). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10234 mūtra explicitly gives Kalasha mūtra, Bshk. mūλ and Western Pahari mūc. The survey lateral/sibilant outcomes fit the tr-cluster urine family; retroflex muṭ and ordinary mute preserve the same noun, with phonetic details left open. Reviewed comparison: Buksa mut “urine” (f_fgdpypslzzy6u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10978 lavaṇa gives the widespread loṇ/lūṇ salt family. Regional retroflex initial ḷ and the northern retained-v lovn do not require a different lexical root; their phonetic details remain in the source transcription. Reviewed comparison: Tor lon “salt” (f_xvicrd62opa64). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7655 pañca explicitly gives Dardic panž/panz and Pashai paĩ/paẽ, alongside Kalasha poñ and Shina poĩ. The survey affricate-to-sibilant and contracted nasal/glide numerals fit this documented five family; exact local phonetic developments remain qualified. Reviewed comparison: Rana patʃ “five” (f_tiogqgdfo4jbw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
